get.description: Public login-page bootstrap endpoint. Returns which ways in this server offers: whether OIDC is configured and enabled, and whether password login is allowed (AUTH_ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN, ignored unless OIDC is fully configured). The login page waits for this single answer before painting, so it never shows a form that then disappears. guest_password_login_enabled is true only where password login is off AND the household actually has split-expense guests, who are exempt from the switch (#847) because they are external people with no account in the household identity provider. It is one bit and says nothing about who or how many; where password login is open the question is moot and the field is false.

post.description:
Body: { expected_count, expected_token? } - the count and the token the confirmation was based on; when the candidate set changed since, the call answers 409 with { data: { count, token } } and changes nothing. With `expected_token` a change of the same size is caught as well (an event assigned by hand while a new import takes its place, or a calendar switched to another person); without it only the count is compared (#1171). Only the confirmed candidate list is processed, each event re-checked when written, so `assigned` can be lower than `expected_count` if events were assigned in the meantime. Response: { data: { assigned } }. Runs in batches so a long history does not block other requests; inherited reminders whose time has passed are marked dismissed. A default assignee only reaches events imported after it was set. This one-off action assigns it to the events already imported from that calendar, across all accounts, but only where an event is not assigned to anyone yet: an assignment made by hand is left alone (#1154). It cannot tell a never-assigned event from one whose assignment was removed by hand. ICS subscriptions are not included.

Returns `{ data: { provider, city, units, current, today, forecast } }` or `{ data: null }` when no provider is configured. `today` carries the calendar day at the weather location plus its high/low; `forecast` holds the following days only. `provider` is `open-meteo` (icon fields are Lucide icon names, `desc` is a `wmo.<code>` i18n key) or `openweathermap` (legacy; icon fields are OWM icon codes, `desc` is localized text).

Household preferences. Language fields: `language` (explicitly chosen data language, or `null` for automatic), plus two read-only values — `language_effective` (what actually applies: `language`, else the language part of `region`, else `en`) and `language_auto` (what automatic mode alone would yield, ignoring `language`). The data language decides in which language the server *stores* content it generates itself - birthday event titles, loan instalments, and the public/school holiday names pulled from OpenHolidays (#946) - so that the API, the ICS feed and calendar sync all agree. Changing it re-syncs the holiday cache on the next run, because that cache holds translated names rather than keys. Weather fields: `weather_provider` (`open-meteo` | `openweathermap` | `null` = auto-detect from env), `weather_lat`, `weather_lon`, `weather_city`, `weather_units` (`metric` | `imperial`). Holiday fields: `holiday_country` (ISO-3166 alpha-2 or `null`), `holiday_subdivision` (e.g. `DE-BY` or `null`), `holiday_group` (school-holiday group for multilingual cantons, e.g. `CH-BE-VS`, or `null`), `holiday_show_public`, `holiday_show_school` (booleans), `holiday_public_color`, `holiday_school_color` (hex), `holiday_last_sync`. Overview fields: `dashboard_widgets` (the tile arrangement that applies to the calling user) and `dashboard_today_glance` (header band on/off), plus `dashboard_widgets_default` / `dashboard_today_glance_default` (what the household published as its default, `dashboard_widgets_default` is `null` when nothing was published) and `dashboard_follows_default` (`true` when the caller has no arrangement of their own and therefore follows the household).

put.description: `language` is admin-only: an ISO-639-1 code with a locale file, or `null`/`""` to fall back to automatic derivation from `region`. Changing it (or `region`, or `date_format`) re-titles the stored birthday events so every channel stays consistent. `timezone` is admin-only too: an IANA zone (validated against ICU, so aliases like `Europe/Kiev` are accepted), or `null`/`""` to fall back to the `TZ` env var, then the host zone, then UTC. It is the household zone used wherever a time carries none of its own - the calendar day server-side jobs call "today", the zone of the exported ICS feed, and the clock time events arrive with in Google and Outlook. The GET response carries both views: `timezone` (what is chosen, `null` for automatic) and `timezone_effective` (what applies, never `null`). Weather fields (`weather_provider`, `weather_lat`, `weather_lon`, `weather_city`, `weather_units`) and holiday fields (`holiday_country`, `holiday_subdivision`, `holiday_group`, `holiday_show_public`, `holiday_show_school`, `holiday_public_color`, `holiday_school_color`) are admin-only. `weather_lat`/`weather_lon` are validated to ±90 / ±180; colors must be 6-digit hex. Module feature toggles `health_cycle_enabled` (show the health cycle tab household-wide) and `rewards_require_approval` (redemptions need admin approval) are admin-only booleans, both default `true`. `health_cycle_enabled_user` is the per-user opt-out for the same tab and is writable by anyone for themselves; it can only narrow the household setting, never widen it. The GET response exposes all three views: `health_cycle_enabled` (household), `health_cycle_enabled_user` (mine) and the read-only `health_cycle_effective` (both combined, which is what the UI renders). Overview fields: `dashboard_widgets` (array of `{id, visible, order, size, options?}`; `options` is stored but not interpreted - the server validates only its shape: a flat object, at most 8 keys, values boolean, finite number, short string or list of short strings) and `dashboard_today_glance` are personal and writable by anyone for themselves; sending `null` for either deletes the personal value, so the caller follows the household default again - including every later change to it. `dashboard_widgets_default` and `dashboard_today_glance_default` are the household default and admin-only; they never overwrite a member who has an arrangement of their own, and `null` removes the default.

post.description: Body: { log_date, flow?, note?, visibility?, symptoms?, basal_temp?, basal_temp_unit?, cervix_mucus?, lh_test?, pregnancy_test?, intimacy?, feelings? }. `cervix_mucus` ∈ dry/sticky/creamy/watery/eggwhite; `lh_test`/`pregnancy_test` ∈ negative/positive; `intimacy` ∈ protected/unprotected/solo. `feelings` is an array from a fixed 7-key set (great/good/neutral/sensitive/sad/irritable/anxious, same as the frontend's MOOD_TYPES) - any other value is a 400, not stored as free text. The legacy single-value `mood` is still accepted and validated against the same fixed set, treated as `feelings: [mood]` when `feelings` is absent. A save whose body includes either `feelings` or `mood` as a key fully replaces the stored feelings rows (delete + re-insert) and sets the `mood` column to NULL; a save that includes neither key leaves both the existing feelings rows and the `mood` column untouched, so an unrelated field change cannot silently clear a frozen legacy mood value. This is NOT the same as `symptoms`: `symptoms` is fully replaced on every save (an omitted `symptoms` array normalizes to empty and clears any existing rows), while `feelings`/`mood` are only replaced when the request actually names one of those two keys.

can_detach_occurrence.description: Legacy occurrence scopes for locally owned series that cannot use linked overrides, including outbound-synced and generated series.

CalendarOccurrenceOnlyMutation.description: Editable fields for one occurrence. Omitted fields inherit their current or series value.

attachment_data.description: A base64 data URL for a replacement attachment, or null to remove it.

CalendarOccurrenceFollowingMutation.description: Editable fields for a successor series. Omitted fields inherit from the original series.

attachment_data.description: A base64 data URL for a replacement attachment, or null to remove it.

password_reset_enabled.description: True when self-service password reset can actually deliver a mail (SMTP configured AND BASE_URL set) and there are passwords to reset at all (AUTH_ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN not switched off). The login page gates the "forgot password" link on this flag so it is never a dead end.

avatar_data.description: PNG, JPEG, or WebP data URL.

onboarding_pending.description: Whether this account still needs the onboarding walkthrough. Derived from the account, not from the browser, so a new device does not repeat it. POST /auth/onboarding-seen clears it.

sso_only.description: Only present on GET /auth/users for administrators: the account carries no password and can only be entered through SSO.

avatar_data.description: PNG, JPEG, or WebP data URL.

sso_only.description: Create the account without a password, so it can only be entered through SSO. Requires OIDC to be configured, and rejects a password sent alongside it. Deliberately explicit rather than inferred from a missing password.

avatar_data.description: PNG, JPEG, or WebP data URL.

password.description: Write-only. Omit or leave empty to keep the current password.

sso_only.description: Switch the account between having a password and entering only through SSO. true clears the password; false requires a password to be sent with it, otherwise the account would be left with no way in at all. Omit to leave unchanged.

Invite.description: A pending invitation. The token hash is never returned.

username.description: Pre-assigned username. When null, the invited person picks one.

expires_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds. Invitations are valid for 7 days.

username.description: Optional. When set, the invited person cannot choose a different one.

system_admin.description: Only true grants the admin role; the value is taken from the invitation, never from the accept request.

send_email.description: Send the invitation by email. Requires SMTP and BASE_URL; check email_sent in the response.

token.description: Plaintext invite token. Returned here and only here - the database holds nothing but its hash, so a lost token cannot be recovered, only revoked and reissued.

email_sent.description: Whether the invitation email actually went out. False when send_email was not requested, SMTP or BASE_URL is missing, or delivery failed - the link must then be passed on by hand.

username.description: Ignored when the invitation already carries one.

display_name.description: Ignored when the invitation already carries one.

subject_user_id.description: Family member whose identity, role, permissions, and data ownership apply to token requests.

scopes.description: Permission allow-list of "module:read"/"module:write" entries. null means no scoping (full role-based access, e.g. legacy tokens). write implies read.

subject_user_id.description: Optional family-member subject. Defaults to the administrator creating the token. Split-expense guests are not eligible.

scopes.description: Optional permission allow-list of "module:read"/"module:write" entries (e.g. ["calendar:write","tasks:read"]). Omit or null for a full-access token. When set, must be non-empty and only contain known scopes. Enforced on both REST and MCP; write implies read.

DmsAccount.description: A configured DMS account. The api_token is never returned; use has_token to check whether one is stored.

has_token.description: Whether an API token is stored for this account

api_token.description: API token for authenticating with the DMS. Write-only; never returned in responses.

DmsLinkResponse.description: The created family_documents row. storage_provider is `external` and storage_backend is `dms` for linked DMS documents.

ExtensionModuleWidget.description: Dashboard widget declared in a third-party module manifest.

entry.description: Protected asset URL for the widget JavaScript entry.

labelKey.description: Short i18n key resolved under extensions.{moduleId}.* (from locales/{locale}.json).

ExtensionModuleCapabilities.description: Normalized capabilities block from module.json (null when not declared or module errored).

apiPrefix.description: Sidecar API prefix. Must be exactly `/api/extensions/<module-id>`.

scopeKey.description: API token scope module key, typically `ext:<module-id>`.

i18n.description: Locale metadata scanned from locales/*.json in the module folder.

defaultLocale.description: Fallback locale when the UI language is not shipped (default en).

availableLocales.description: Locale files present in the module.

coreLocales.description: All locales supported by Yuvomi core.

weekdays.description: Comma-separated RRULE BYDAY codes (e.g. "MO,TH") for recurrence_kind=weekly; exactly ONE code (e.g. "MO") for recurrence_kind=monthly_ordinal_weekday. Null for monthly_fixed_day.

month_day.description: recurrence_kind=monthly_fixed_day: a day-of-month (1-31), or -1 for the last day. recurrence_kind=monthly_ordinal_weekday: the ORDINAL POSITION of the chosen weekday - -1 (last) or 1-4 (nth), reusing this same column for a different meaning (#1063 Phase 9). Null for weekly.

active.description: 0 = paused; contributes no occurrences until reactivated.

weekdays.description: weekly: an array of BYDAY codes, e.g. ["MO","TH"]. monthly_ordinal_weekday: a single code string, e.g. "MO".

month_day.description: monthly_fixed_day: 1-31 or -1. monthly_ordinal_weekday: the ordinal position, -1 (last) or 1-4 (nth).

replacement_date.description: null means this occurrence is explicitly skipped.
A date to move this occurrence to, or null to skip it.

original_summary.description: The imported event's own SUMMARY text; present when kind is "import".

coalesced.description: true when more than one origin (e.g. a schedule and a one-off) supplies this same date.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the ICS text behind the currently committed snapshot.

version.description: Bumped on every committed (re)import; the concurrency guard for reimport/commit.

last_success_at.description: Only updated on a successful commit; a failed attempt never clears it.

needs_refresh.description: true when this source has no mapped pickup on or after today (invariant #6) - derived, not stored.

url.description: kind=url only. A credential: omitted entirely for a caller without module write access, never merely masked.

next_attempt_at.description: kind=url only. null while needs_mapping is set - the scheduler skips the source until a reviewed refresh.

consecutive_failures.description: kind=url only. Drives exponential backoff; reset to 0 on any successful fetch.

needs_mapping.description: kind=url only. Content changed but could not auto-commit (an unmapped label or unresolved blocking diagnostic); resolved only by a reviewed refresh.

event_key.description: Present on a "blocking" diagnostic; pass it back in skip_event_keys on commit to exclude the affected event and unblock the rest of the file.

suggested_type_id.description: A same-name (case-insensitive) match against an existing type; a convenience default only, never applied on its own.

remembered_type_id.description: The type this label was mapped to on the source's last commit, on a re-import preview.

digest.description: sha256 of what this preview shows (candidates/labels/diagnostics), not of the raw ICS bytes; pass it back as preview_digest on commit. A URL source may be re-fetched between preview and commit - this digest still matches as long as the parsed result is unchanged.

source_id.description: null for a fresh import preview.

expected_version.description: The source's current version, for a re-import preview; pass it back as expected_version on commit.

WasteImportMappingDecision.description: Exactly one of type_id / new_type / ignored must be set. One decision is required per distinct label reported by the preview.

ics.description: The raw ICS file text (re-parsed on commit; never trusts a client-supplied candidate list).

name.description: Required for a fresh import (POST /import/commit); defaults to the existing name on a re-import.

skip_event_keys.description: Blocking-diagnostic event_key values explicitly acknowledged and excluded.

preview_digest.description: The digest returned by the matching preview; a mismatch (the parsed content actually changed since that preview) is refused with 409.

expected_version.description: Required on a re-import commit; the source's version as last seen in a preview (409 on mismatch).

coalesced.description: Informational: how many accepted pickups land on a date a manual schedule/one-off (or another source) already provides for the same type.

url.description: https:// only by default; http:// is accepted only under the operator opt-in WASTE_SOURCE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK.

outcome.description: committed: every label had a remembered decision, applied via the same atomic path as a file re-import. unchanged: a conditional GET reported no change (304). needs_mapping: content changed but at least one label (or blocking diagnostic) has no remembered decision - see source.needs_mapping and the preview field. error: the fetch failed - see source.last_error.

type_name.description: Only present on GET (list); PUT's response is scoped to the one type_id already in the URL.

offset_days.description: Lead time before the pickup, in days. Bounded 0-14.

delivery_time.description: Household-local HH:MM the reminder is delivered at.

url.description: Public, unauthenticated .ics URL. Rotates when regenerated.

type_ids.description: Optional type selection. null (default) means every active type.
Waste type ids to include, or null to include every active type again.

pattern.description: Normalized source label this pattern matches.

source_name.description: Only present on export, informational only.

status.description: applicable: will be applied on commit. unchanged: source mapping already matches. unmatched_pattern: no mapping in this source has this pattern. unmatched_type: no waste type in this household has this name. ambiguous_type: more than one waste type shares this name and none of them is the mapping's own current type - never guessed at, resolve the name collision (rename one of the types) before this entry can apply.

profile_digest.description: Pass back unchanged on commit; a mismatch means the profile changed since this preview.
